quizName: DMV Practice Test #10 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Passengers should:

options.text: Sit as far back as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean with the operator.
questions.explanation: Tell your passenger to lean with you when turning. They should hold onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: When it is obvious that you are going to turn, you:

options.text: Do not need to use a turn signal.
Should still use a turn signal.
Only need to use a turn signal if pedestrians are nearby.
Only need to use a turn signal at a stop light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should still use a turn signal.
questions.explanation: Always use a turn signal every time you turn or change lanes. Use it even if you think others can see what you are doing. Other vehicles may be hidden from view.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Rectangular signs show road rules like speed limits. They are white with black letters or symbols. You must follow all rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: Before carrying a passenger in traffic for the first time, you should:

options.text: Practice riding on a quiet road.
Flash your lights so others can see you.
Practice riding on the road shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Practice riding on a quiet road.
questions.explanation: Before taking a passenger or heavy load on a busy road, practice on a quiet road first. This helps you get used to how your motorcycle feels with extra weight.

questions.question: When preparing to pass another vehicle on the left, you should ride in:

options.text: The left side of the lane.
The right side of the lane.
Either the right or center portions of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The left side of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride on the left side of your lane when preparing to pass. This position gives you the best view of the passing lane ahead.

questions.question: Your lane position should:

options.text: Protect your lane from other drivers.
Give you a nice view of scenery.
Place you in other drivers' blind spots.
Hide your intentions from other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protect your lane from other drivers.
questions.explanation: Good lane position helps your safety in many ways. It keeps you out of blind spots, helps you see and be seen, avoids road hazards, avoids wind from other vehicles, and gives you an escape route. Position yourself so other drivers will not try to share your lane.

questions.question: To be effective, an eye or face shield should be all of the following, except:
questions.correctAnswerText: Airtight.
questions.explanation: Good eye protection must be free of scratches, resist breaking, give a clear side view, fasten securely, allow air to pass through, and fit over eyeglasses or sunglasses.

questions.question: More than half of all motorcycle crashes:
questions.correctAnswerText: Involve inexperienced riders.
questions.explanation: More than half of motorcycle crashes involve riders with less than six months of experience. Most crashes happen during the day at low speeds.

questions.question: A major effect of alcohol consumption is:
questions.correctAnswerText: Slowed body functions.
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant. It slows down both your physical and mental abilities.

questions.question: It is recommended that a motorcyclist:

options.text: Change power suddenly in a turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift gears before a turn.
questions.explanation: Change gears before entering a turn, not during the turn.

questions.question: A windshield:

options.text: Is a good substitute for a face shield.
Does not fully protect your eyes from the wind.
Should be used on windy days.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not fully protect your eyes from the wind.
questions.explanation: A windshield does not provide the same protection as goggles or a face shield. Most windshields will not protect your eyes from wind.

questions.question: As the motorcycle's weight moves forward while braking, you:

options.text: Can apply the front brake harder.
Should use less pressure on the front brake.
Can apply the rear brake harder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can apply the front brake harder.
questions.explanation: When your weight shifts forward while braking, the front wheel has more traction. This means you can apply the front brake harder.

questions.question: When adjusting your mirrors, you should focus on:

options.text: The road behind and to the side of your motorcycle.
The road in front of your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road behind and to the side of your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors to see the lane behind you and the lane next to you. A mirror may show part of your arm or shoulder, but the road behind and beside you is most important.

questions.question: When changing lanes, riders should:

options.text: Use only their mirrors to check for other vehicles.
Turn their head to look for traffic behind them.
Slam on the brakes to let vehicles in their blind spot pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn their head to look for traffic behind them.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like other vehicles. Always turn your head to check for traffic before changing lanes.

questions.question: Passengers should:

options.text: Sit as far back on the bike as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean as the operator leans.
questions.explanation: Passengers should sit directly behind the operator and lean when the operator leans. Sit as far forward as possible without crowding the operator, and hold onto the operator's waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: When approaching railroad tracks that cross your lane at an angle, it is usually:

options.text: Safest to ride straight within your lane to cross the tracks.
Dangerous to ride straight within your lane to cross the tracks.
Not safe to cross tracks on a motorcycle.
Safest to cross the tracks by riding on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Safest to ride straight within your lane to cross the tracks.
questions.explanation: Cross angled railroad tracks by riding straight within your lane. Turning to cross at a 90-degree angle is dangerous because you could enter another lane of traffic.

questions.question: When you ride a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through turns.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn just your head and eyes to look through turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just your head and eyes to look through turns.
questions.explanation: When turning, look where you want to go by turning only your head. Keep your knees against the gas tank for balance while turning. Keep your arms slightly bent when holding the handgrips.

questions.question: A properly-fitted motorcycle:

options.text: Allows the rider to touch the ground with their feet while seated.
Has a seat even with the rider's waist.
Has a seat that is 10 inches above the rider's waist.
Has a seat that is 10 inches below the rider's waist.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allows the rider to touch the ground with their feet while seated.
questions.explanation: A properly-fitted motorcycle lets you touch the ground with your feet while sitting on the seat. Keep your feet firmly on the footrests while riding.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should:

options.text: Ride a little more slowly than usual.
Ride a little faster than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride a little more slowly than usual.
questions.explanation: With a passenger's extra weight, your motorcycle sits lower. Ride slower than usual, especially through curves, corners, and over bumps. The extra weight makes acceleration, slowing down, and stopping take longer. Keep a larger space cushion when carrying a passenger.

questions.question: The front brake supplies how much of a motorcycle's stopping power?
questions.correctAnswerText: About three-quarters
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides about three-quarters of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: What color are warning signs with black lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: When a group of motorcycle riders passes another vehicle on a two-lane road, how should they pass?

options.text: Pass in a staggered formation with several riders passing at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pass one at a time.
questions.explanation: Riders should pass one at a time on a two-lane road. Each rider must finish their pass before the next rider begins.

questions.question: What should you do to control your motorcycle while turning?

options.text: Increase your speed before entering the turn.
Look through the turn to see what is ahead.
Come to a complete stop before entering the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look through the turn to see what is ahead.
questions.explanation: Look through the turn by turning only your head. Slow down before turning and lean your motorcycle in the right direction.

questions.question: What must you do when passing another vehicle?

options.text: You must complete the pass without exceeding the speed limit.
You may complete the pass in a no passing zone if the pass was started before the no passing zone began.
You may exceed the speed limit.
You should pass on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must complete the pass without exceeding the speed limit.
questions.explanation: All passes must follow the speed limit and only happen where passing is allowed.

questions.question: On which surface does a motorcycle have the best traction?
questions.correctAnswerText: Dry pavement
questions.explanation: Dry pavement gives the best traction. Wet pavement, gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lines, and metal covers are all hazardous for motorcycles.
